# 2. Data Audit

#### Removing Duplicate Rows

```{r}
hotels_raw <- hotels_raw |> distinct()
mean(hotels_raw$is_canceled)  # overall cancellation rate
```

- After duplicates are removed, we are left with:

  - 87,396 rows/bookings

  - overall cancellation rate of 27.5% (class imbalance will need to be addressed later)

Checking data point for missing Market Segment

```{r}
hotels_raw |> filter(arrival_date_month == "August" & arrival_date_year == 2015 & arrival_date_week_number == 32 & is.na(children))
```

#### Checking for missing values

```{r}
colSums(is.na(hotels_raw))
hotels_raw |> summarize(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.))))
```

The variables with missing data are:

- children - 4

- country - 452

- market_segment - 0 (2 Undefined)

- distribution channel - 0 (5 Undefined)

- company - 82137

## Dropping leakage variables

reservation_status and reservation_status_date give the outcome (we just need the var is_canceled). assigned_room_type and booking_changes are updated after the booking is made.

```{r}
hotels_raw <- hotels_raw |>
    select(-c(reservation_status, reservation_status_date, assigned_room_type, booking_changes))
```

## Changing data types

```{r}
str(hotels_raw)

# Data documentation tells us "Undefined" = "SC"
table(hotels_raw$meal) # "Undefined" level
hotels_raw <- hotels_raw |>
    mutate(meal = case_when(meal == "Undefined" ~ "SC", 
                            # Combining Full Board with Hald Board since the categories are such a small percentage of the data and we want to reduce                                   categories
                            meal == "FB" ~ "HB", 
                            TRUE ~ meal),
           meal = factor(meal, levels = c("SC", "BB", "HB"), ordered = TRUE))

mean(is.na(hotels_raw$company)) # percent of company variable missing (94%)
hotels_raw <- hotels_raw |>
    mutate(has_company = ifelse(is.na(company), 0, 1)) 
        

hotels_raw <- hotels_raw |>
    mutate(across(c(hotel, is_canceled, country, market_segment, distribution_channel,
                    is_repeated_guest, reserved_room_type, deposit_type, agent,
                    customer_type, has_company), as.factor),
           arrival_date_month = factor(arrival_date_month, levels = month.name, ordered = TRUE))

# Confirm
str(hotels_raw)
```

**Ordinal:** arrival_date_month, meal (SC \< BB \< HB)

**Nominal:** hotel, country, market_segment, distribution_channel, reserved_room_type, deposit_type, agent, customer_type

**Binary:** is_canceled (target), is_repeated_guest, has_company

## Modifying other data problems / Engineering new features

```{r}
hotels_raw |> skim()
```

```{r}
# Problems found in the raw data 
table(hotels_raw$market_segment) # "Undefined" level
table(hotels_raw$distribution_channel) # "Undefined" level
summary(hotels_raw$adr) # negative min, extreme max
mean(is.na(hotels_raw$company)) # percent of company variable missing (94%)
sum(hotels_raw$adults + hotels_raw$children + hotels_raw$babies == 0, na.rm = TRUE) # 166 zero-guest bookings
```

```{r}
hotels_raw <- hotels_raw |>
    mutate(market_segment = replace(market_segment, market_segment == "Undefined", NA), # 2 "Undefined" turning into NA
           distribution_channel = replace(distribution_channel, distribution_channel == "Undefined", NA), # 5 "Undefined" turning into NA
           adr = replace(adr, adr < 0 | adr > 1000, NA), # ASSUMPTION: impossible / extreme nightly rates
           agent = as.factor(replace_na(as.character(agent), "None")),   # ASSUMPTION: no agent = booked directly
           total_nights = stays_in_weekend_nights + stays_in_week_nights, # new variable
           total_guests = adults + coalesce(children, 0) + babies) |> # new variable
    select(-company) # 94.3% of this variable is missing 

# ASSUMPTION: bookings with zero guests are data errors
hotels_raw <- hotels_raw |> filter(total_guests > 0) 

# Drop unused levels 
hotels_raw <- hotels_raw |> droplevels()
```

- After this data cleaning, we are now left with:

  -  87,230 bookings

  - 29 potential variables

  - 27.5% overall cancellation rate (same as above)

## Decision Tree to help consolidate levels

- They both only return one node (even when we lower the cp threshold)

  - Becuause no category has more than 50% cancellations

  - Not necessary

```{r}
# Market Segment
ms_tree <- rpart(is_canceled ~ market_segment, data = hotels_raw)
plot(as.party(ms_tree))

# Distribution Channel
dc_tree <- rpart(is_canceled ~ distribution_channel, data = hotels_raw)
plot(as.party(dc_tree))
```

## Re-categorizing levels of country and removing undesired variables

```{r}
europe <- c("GBR", "ESP", "FRA", "IRL", "DEU", "ITA", "BEL", "NLD", "CHE", "AUT",
            "SWE", "NOR", "DNK", "FIN", "ISL", "POL", "CZE", "SVK", "HUN", "ROU",
            "BGR", "GRC", "HRV", "SVN", "SRB", "BIH", "MNE", "MKD", "ALB", "EST",
            "LVA", "LTU", "LUX", "MLT", "CYP", "UKR", "BLR", "RUS", "AND", "MCO",
            "SMR", "LIE", "GIB", "JEY", "GGY", "IMN", "FRO")
# Left out: Turkey (TUR), Georgia (GEO), Armenia (ARM), Azerbaijan (AZE) and Kazakhstan (KAZ), which are partly in Asia. Also French overseas territories like Guadeloupe (GLP) and Mayotte (MYT), which aren’t in Europe geographically

hotels_raw <- hotels_raw |>
    mutate(country = case_when(is.na(country) | country == "Unknown" ~ "Unknown", #447 total NA
                               country == "PRT" ~ "Portugal",
                               country %in% europe ~ "Europe",
                               TRUE ~ "Foreign"),
           country = as.factor(country)) |> 
    select(-c(meal, agent, reserved_room_type, arrival_date_year)) # drop these variables due to too many levels and/or sparse data; we do not believe these variables will help us out.

hotels_raw |> group_by(country) |> summarise(n = n(), cancel_rate = mean(is_canceled == 1))
```

- We dropped meal, agent, reserved_room_type, arrival_date_year

  - Too many levels

  - No documentation on categories/not interpretable

  - Sparse data

- We reorganized country to be either Portugal, Europe minus Portugal, or Foreign/Other to reduce the number of categoried

  - The hotels are in Portugal so we thought this would make sense

## Variable Importance

### Categorical Inputs

```{r}
hotels_raw |> 
    summarize(across(where(is.factor) & !c(is_canceled), ~ chisq.test(., hotels_raw$is_canceled)$p.value)) |> 
    unlist() |> 
    sort()
```

- The 4 with a p-value of `0.000000e+00` are country, market_segment, distribution_channel and deposit_type

### Numeric Inputs

Numerical input - t stat

```{r}
hotels_raw |> 
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), ~ t.test(. ~ is_canceled)$p.value)) |>
    unlist() |> 
    sort()
```

- This shows that the top 2 numeric variables based on importance are lead_time and adr (average daily rate)

Numeric input - area under ROC curve for predicting target, using `caret`

```{r}
hotels_raw |> 
    select(is_canceled, where(is.numeric)) |>  
    filterVarImp(hotels_raw$is_canceled) |>  
    slice(-1) |> 
    arrange(desc(X1)) 
```

- SAME TOP VARS AS ABOVE: This shows that the top 2 variables based on importance are lead_time and adr (average daily rate)

## Transformations

```{r}
num_vars <- hotels_raw |> select(where(is.numeric)) |> names() 

hotels_raw |> select_if(is.numeric) |> skewness(na.rm = TRUE)
for (v in num_vars) {
    p <- ggplot(hotels_raw, aes(.data[[v]])) +
        geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
        ggtitle(v)
    print(p)
}
TransformParams <- hotels_raw |>
    preProcess(method = "YeoJohnson")
TransformParams$yj # based on YeoJohnson and looking at skewness/graph distributions, we will log transform lead_time, stays_in_weekend_nights, stays_in_week_nights, total_nights, total_guests, adr by log(x + 1)

hotels_xf <- hotels_raw

hotels_xf <- hotels_xf |>
    mutate(across(c(lead_time, stays_in_weekend_nights,
          stays_in_week_nights, adr,
          total_nights, total_guests),
        ~ log(. + 1)
    )) 

hotels_xf |> select_if(is.numeric) |> skewness(na.rm = TRUE) #all transformed variables have improvement in skewness besides adr, may not be worth transforming

for (v in num_vars) {
    p <- ggplot(hotels_xf, aes(.data[[v]])) +
        geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
        ggtitle(v)
    print(p)
} # visibily all improved, besides adr, so we will keep the transformation on all transformed variables, besides adr


# Trying the Box-Cox Transformation on ADR
hotels_raw |>  
    as.data.frame() |>  
    predict(TransformParams, newdata = _) |> 
    as_tibble() |> 
    ggplot() + 
    aes(x = adr) + 
    geom_histogram()

hotels_raw |>  
    mutate(adr = sqrt(adr)) |> 
    ggplot() + 
    aes(x = adr) + 
    geom_histogram()


hotels_xf <- hotels_raw

hotels_xf_final <- hotels_xf |>
    mutate(across(c(lead_time, stays_in_weekend_nights,
          stays_in_week_nights,
          total_nights, total_guests),
        ~ log(. + 1)), 
        adr = sqrt(adr))

```

- After exploring potential transformations, we ended up LOG TRANSFORMING the variables:

  - lead_time

  - stays_in_weekend_nights

  - stays_in_week_nights

  - total_nights

  - total_guests

- SRT TRANSFORMING

  - adr

## Imputation

Our dataset is already complete case (we dropped the 7 observations with NAs)

For logistic regression AND tree based models: our dataset will be the same for all models since since we decided not to impute for the 7 missing values, rather we dropped these observations

- So, all models can learn from the same points
